summary:
The Sleeping Explorers is an illustrated digital children's book designed to transform technical and historical space mission data into an engaging educational adventure for school-aged audiences.

> Following the journey of young astronaut Luna and her robotic co-pilot ASTRO, the project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by humanizing the inactive hardware left by NASA on the Moon and Mars (such as Apollo descent stages and Martian rovers). Rather than labeling them merely as discarded debris, the narrative honors them as silent monuments and pioneers that enabled humanity's greatest scientific discoveries.

> Its significance lies in bridging space history with sustainability: by connecting historical exploration with the UN 2030 Agenda's Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 4, 9, and 12), it inspires the next generation to envision future space exploration rooted in technological innovation, circular design, and environmental responsibility.
details:
Luna & ASTRO: A Cosmic Cleanup Mission

What does your project do or how does it work?

Our project is an educational and interactive story for elementary school students. It follows Luna, a young space explorer, and ASTRO, her friendly robot companion, as they travel through space and discover the objects that humanity has left behind during decades of space exploration.

Through their journey, Luna and ASTRO explore different locations, including Earth orbit, the Moon, and Mars, where students learn about spacecraft, rovers, landers, satellites, and other human-made objects associated with space exploration.

The story introduces the problem of space debris in a simple and engaging way. Children learn that, just as we should not leave garbage in our schools, parks, or communities, we also need to take responsibility for the objects we send into space.

The project transforms scientific and historical information into a narrative experience that combines storytelling, visual learning, space exploration, environmental awareness, and technology.

The story concludes by challenging students to become problem-solvers themselves:

“If you were an astronaut, what would you invent to keep space clean?”

This question encourages students to imagine and design their own technological solutions.

What benefits does your project offer?

The main benefit is to make science, technology, engineering, and space exploration accessible and exciting for elementary school students.

The project helps students:

  • Understand what space debris is.
  • Learn about the history of human space exploration.
  • Recognize the importance of protecting the space environment.
  • Develop environmental awareness and responsibility.
  • Strengthen creativity and scientific curiosity.
  • Practice problem-solving and critical thinking.
  • Discover the relationship between technology and environmental sustainability.
  • Become interested in science, engineering, robotics, programming, and space exploration.
  • Imagine technological solutions to real-world problems.

What is the expected impact of the project?

The expected impact is primarily educational, environmental, and technological.

In the short term, the project seeks to spark children's curiosity about science and space while helping them understand that human activities can create environmental challenges beyond Earth.

In the medium and long term, the project aims to encourage a culture of responsibility toward technology and the environment. Students learn that when we design, use, and dispose of technological objects, our decisions can have consequences that extend beyond our planet.

The project also seeks to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, programmers, astronauts, and innovators to develop sustainable solutions for future space exploration.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

The project was developed primarily using digital tools for storytelling, visual content creation, and educational resources.

Artificial intelligence generative tools were used to support the development of visual concepts, illustrations, characters, and narrative elements for the Luna and ASTRO universe.

The project also has the potential to be expanded through artificial intelligence, robotics, programming, sensors, and interactive simulations, allowing students to participate in technological challenges related to space debris.

At this stage, the central technological component is the integration of artificial intelligence, digital storytelling, scientific information, and visual learning, rather than the construction of a physical device.

In what way is your project creative?

The creativity of the project comes from combining three elements that are often presented separately:

children's storytelling + space exploration + an environmental and technological challenge.

Instead of explaining space debris through a traditional lesson, the project turns the subject into an adventure.

Luna and ASTRO serve as guides who allow children to discover the problem while traveling through different space environments.

Another creative element is that students are not simply spectators. They become part of the mission.

At the end of the story, they are challenged to imagine their own solutions, such as:

  • A space-debris collection robot.
  • A self-repairing satellite.
  • A system for recovering and reusing discarded rocket components.
  • A technology capable of identifying and tracking space debris.

In this way, the story becomes the starting point for project-based learning, creativity, engineering thinking, and innovation.

What factors did your team take into consideration?

Our team considered several important factors during the development of the project:

  1. The age of the target audience — The language, characters, images, and situations were designed to be accessible and engaging for elementary school students.
  2. Children's natural interest in space — Astronauts, robots, planets, spacecraft, and exploration were incorporated to capture their attention.
  3. The space-debris problem — The topic was presented as a real challenge while keeping the explanation understandable for children.
  4. Environmental education — The story connects space debris with a familiar idea: just as we should not throw garbage on the ground, we should also take responsibility for what we send into space.
  5. The United Nations 2030 Agenda — The project incorporates concepts related to education, innovation, responsible consumption, environmental responsibility, and partnerships.
  6. Accessibility of scientific knowledge — Complex scientific and historical information was transformed into an understandable narrative using characters and visual elements.
  7. Active student participation — Students are encouraged to imagine, design, and propose solutions rather than simply receive information.
  8. Future scalability — The project can evolve into a more interactive educational experience incorporating artificial intelligence, robotics, programming, sensors, and simulations.

Overall project vision

Luna & ASTRO: A Cosmic Cleanup Mission transforms a real challenge associated with space exploration into an educational adventure for children.

The project connects space exploration, environmental awareness, artificial intelligence, creativity, and the United Nations 2030 Agenda in a format designed to inspire young learners.

Our goal is to help children move from readers to explorers, and from explorers to future engineers and innovators.

The central message of the project is:

“If we want to explore new worlds, we must first learn how to take care of the world we already have.”
